**You need a power station with at least 1,200W of surge output and about 1,000–2,000Wh of capacity.** The surge rating lets the compressor start. The capacity decides how long the fridge keeps running.

I fully read only one of the three pages I fetched, HomeGridHQ's [refrigerator sizing guide](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/). The Anker and powerstations.reviews pages were too large to load, and I couldn't open the saved copies. The figures below come from HomeGridHQ alone. I haven't cross-checked them.

**Fridge power draw (HomeGridHQ's figures)**
- A typical full-size fridge draws about 100–200W while the compressor runs.
- It surges to roughly 900–1,200W for a moment when the compressor starts.
- Because the compressor cycles on and off, the average is only about 30–50W. HomeGridHQ plans around 150W running, 1,200W surge and a 35% duty cycle, which works out to about 62Wh per hour.
- Mini fridges and chest freezers need less. Their start surge is about 600–800W.

**Sizing by outage length (door kept closed)**

| Capacity | Approximate runtime |
|---|---|
| ~1,000Wh | ~16 hours |
| ~2,000Wh | ~32 hours |
| ~4,000Wh | 2.5+ days |

**Things to watch**
- Check the continuous and surge output ratings, not just the capacity. Small units under 500Wh often can't absorb the compressor's start surge.
- Food in a closed fridge is only safe for about 4 hours without power. A full, closed freezer lasts 24–48 hours (USDA guidance, as quoted by HomeGridHQ).
- Add up any other devices you plan to run, because they shorten the runtime.

**Options from that guide (prices as listed there)**
- **About one day, budget:** [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D7PPG25F?tag=homegridhq-20), 1,070Wh, $499, about 17 hours.
- **About one day, budget:** [Anker SOLIX C1000](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C5C89QKZ?tag=homegridhq-20), 1,056Wh, $470, about 17 hours.
- **A day and a third:** [Bluetti AC200L](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac200l), 2,048Wh, $899, about 33 hours. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/lab/V1/bluetti-ac200l) lists a code, AFF5OFF, for $44.95 off. I couldn't verify that code.
- **A day and a third:** [EcoFlow Delta 3 Max](https://us.ecoflow.com/products/ecoflow-delta-3-max-portable-power-station-2048wh), 2,048Wh, $879, about 33 hours.
- **Multi-day:** [EcoFlow Delta Pro 3](https://us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-pro-3-portable-power-station), 4,096Wh, $2,799, about 2.8 days.

If you tell me your fridge's size and how long your outages usually last, I can narrow this to one or two picks.

 What Size Power Station Do You Need to Run a Refrigerator?
 Verified October 2026  Manufacturer + DOE typical ratings. [Methodology](/about/)
 Quick answer: To run a refrigerator you need a power station with at least 1,200W of surge (to start the compressor) and about 1,000Wh of capacity to cover most of a day. A modern full-size fridge uses 100-200 watts while the compressor runs , surges to 900-1,200 watts at compressor start, and averages 30-50W over a day thanks to cycling. For backup sizing, plan around 150W running, 1,200W surge, and a ~35% duty cycle. 
 Refrigerator wattage by type
 Type Running watts Compressor start 
 Mini fridge 80W 600W 
 Top-freezer 18 cu ft 120W 1,000W 
 French door 25 cu ft 180W 1,200W 
 Garage chest freezer 100W 800W 
 Refrigerators are the most common reason to buy backup power - a fridge holds $200-400 of food, and the USDA says food is unsafe after 4 hours above 40°F with the door closed. The good news: fridges are cheap to back up. At a 35% duty cycle, one uses only ~62Wh per hour after inverter losses. Keep the door shut and even a 1kWh station protects your food most of a day. The number that disqualifies small inverters is the compressor start surge - clear 1,200W and you're safe.
 How long real power stations run a refrigerator
 Computed from each unit's rated capacity at 85% inverter efficiency and a 35% duty cycle (150W running, 1,200W start). Units whose continuous output can't run it, whose motor-start surge can't start it are excluded. Where a maker's headline surge only applies to resistive loads, we size starts off continuous output.
